  # Downloading Census Data

```{r}
tracts <- get_decennial(geography = "tract",
                           variables = "H1_001N",
                           state = params$states,
                           year = 2020,
                           geometry = TRUE)
```

# Obtaining Demographic Data from US Census

```{r}
# Median income in past 12 months: B06011_001 (individual income), B19013_001 (household income)

income <- get_acs(
  state = params$states,
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B19013_001",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide",
  year = 2020)

income <- st_drop_geometry(income)
```

https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/pl/groups/P2.html

```{r}
white_p <- get_decennial(
  state = params$states,
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "P2_005N",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide",
  year = 2020)

# previously used B02001_002 (and was set to get_acs)

white_p <- st_drop_geometry(white_p)

white_population <- sum(white_p$P2_005N)

white_population
```

```{r}
black_p <- get_decennial(
  state = params$states,
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "P2_006N",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide",
  year = 2020)

# B02001_003 via get_acs() previously

black_p <- st_drop_geometry(black_p)

black_population <- sum(black_p$P2_006N)

black_population
```

```{r}
hispanic_p <- get_decennial(
```


# Compiling Walksheds_DF

Note: right now walksheds_df has the same name as the df file from notebook-01 (should I change one?)

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  left_join(income |> select(GEOID, B19013_001E), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(white_p |> select(GEOID, P2_005N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(black_p |> select(GEOID, P2_006N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(hispanic_p |> select(GEOID, P2_002N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(asian_p |> select(GEOID, P2_008N), by = "GEOID")
```

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  rename(household_income = B19013_001E) |>
  rename(white_pop = P2_005N) |>
  rename(black_pop = P2_006N) |>
  rename(hispanic_pop = P2_002N) |>
  rename(asian_pop = P2_008N) |>
  mutate() |>
  rename(tract_name = NAME) |> # should I keep this to change from NAME to tract_name? or remove altogether
  rename(housing_count = HousingCount) |>
  rename(primary_ruca = PrimaryRUCA) |>
  rename(population_count = PopulationCount) |>
  rename(walkshed_area = WalkshedArea)
```

How to change order of columns (if necessary)?

```{r}
# Walksheds Dataframe
save(walksheds_df, 
     file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data/walkshed_dataframes/{params$city}_walksheds_df.rda"),
     compress = "bzip2")
```

```{r}
ggplot(walksheds_df, aes(fill = (white_pop/population_count))) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Portion of tract population that
is non-Hispanic white only")
```

```{r}
RUCA_exclude <- c(2:6)

RUCA_1_tracts <- walksheds_df |>
  filter(!(primary_ruca %in% RUCA_exclude))
```

```{r}
ggplot(RUCA_1_tracts, aes(fill = (white_pop/population_count))) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Portion of tract population that
is non-Hispanic white only")
```

```{r}
labs(fill = "Portion of tract population that
is non-Hispanic black only")
```

Note that the graphs below are not population-weighted.

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  mutate(white_prop = white_pop/population_count)
```

```{r}
ggscatter(walksheds_df, x = "white_prop", y = "walkshed_area", add = "reg.line", shape = 19, size = 1, xlab = "Proportion of White Population in Census Tract", ylab = "Area of Walkshed in Square Meters", font.label = c(5, "plain", "black")) +
  stat_cor(label.x = 0.75, label.y = 2000000) #label placement
```

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  mutate(black_prop = black_pop/population_count)
```

```{r}
ggscatter(walksheds_df, x = "black_prop", y = "walkshed_area", add = "reg.line", shape = 19, size = 1, xlab = "Proportion of Black Population in Census Tract", ylab = "Area of Walkshed in Square Meters", font.label = c(5, "plain", "black")) +
  stat_cor(label.x = 0.75, label.y = 2000000) #label placement
```

```{r}
ggscatter(walksheds_df, x = "household_income", y = "walkshed_area", add = "reg.line", shape = 19, size = 1, xlab = "Average Household Income in Census Tract (Annual, USD)", ylab = "Area of Walkshed in Square Meters", xlim = c(0, 155000)) +
  stat_cor(label.x = 120000, label.y = 2000000) #label placement
```

How to include population weighting (especially for the R value)?
e.g. (black pop / total pop) * black pop ?

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  mutate(white_prop_weighted = white_pop/population_count*white_pop)
```

```{r}
ggscatter(walksheds_df, x = "white_prop_weighted", y = "walkshed_area", add = "reg.line", shape = 19, size = 1, xlab = "Weighted White Population Proportion in Census Tract", ylab = "Area of Walkshed in Square Meters", font.label = c(5, "plain", "black")) +
  stat_cor(label.x = 0.75, label.y = 2000000) #label placement
```

^ But it doesn't put extra emphasis on those tracts with a higher weighted population and it doesn't compare how much of the tract has a black population in comparison.

```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  mutate(black_prop_weighted = black_pop/population_count*black_pop)
```

```{r}
ggscatter(walksheds_df, x = "black_prop_weighted", y = "walkshed_area", add = "reg.line", shape = 19, size = 1, xlab = "Weighted Black Population Proportion in Census Tract", ylab = "Area of Walkshed in Square Meters", font.label = c(5, "plain", "black")) +
  stat_cor(label.x = 0.75, label.y = 2000000) #label placement
```
